newsitem.title: USA: Late lawsuit filed vs tobacco industry by unions.
newsitem.headline: Late lawsuit filed vs tobacco industry by unions.

text.p: Two private-sector union health and welfare funds sued the tobacco industry in federal court with the industry on the brink of a landmark settlement with 40 states.
The lawsuit was filed Thursday on behalf of the Transport Workers Union (TWU) New York City Private Bus Lines Health Benefit Trust and the Labourers Local 17 Health Benefit Fund.
It seeks recovery of funds spent treating tobacco-related illnesses of union members -- the same compensation sought by the 40 states that sued the industry on behalf of their Medicaid plans.

The union funds seek status as a class action and qualification under federal racketeer-influenced corrupt organisation (RICO) law. A class action could cover hundreds of funds representing hundreds of thousands of union members.

Similar lawsuits, filed on behalf of union funds whose members are subject to private-employer collective bargaining agreements, have been filed in Washington state, California, Iowa, Illinois and Massachusetts, according to Steve Fineman, an attorney for the funds.

"We are compeletely distinct in the sense that we don't find this entire segment of the health field covered within these settlement talks" in Washington, D.C., Arthur Luxenberg, another attorney for the unions, said Friday.
"This litigation and the settlements being announced on behalf of the states have nothing to do with the individual pension funds that expended the same amount of funds," Luxenberg said.
He said that if the private union health funds were invited to join the settlement process, the plaintiffs would consider that option.

The lawsuit alleges the tobacco companies conspired to wilfully and intentionally engage in fraudulent conduct to conceal and misrepresent the addictiveness and harmfulness of cigarettes and smokeless tobacco, and conspired to suppress the development of safer cigarettes.
The lawsuit also alleges the companies and the industry fraudulently promised to conduct objective research and disclose accurate results of the research.
Officials of the tobacco industry could not immediately be reached for comment.
